company_items.summary: Citigroup posted a strong Q3 EPS beat of $2.85 vs. the Street's $2.65, up 27% year-over-year, on slightly higher revenue of $23.85B vs. $23.72B expected and better expense controls with the efficiency ratio improving 290 basis points to 59%. Within the investment bank, FICC rose 4% to $4.38B, IB fees surged 9% to $1.35B, and Equity Underwriting jumped 77% year-over-year. Full-year guidance was nudged higher on both net interest income — now expected up mid-to-high 6% vs. prior 5-6% — and ROTCE, now guided to 11% vs. the prior 10-11% range.

sectors: Large-cap banks showing solid Q3 momentum with Citigroup's beat driven by investment banking strength, expense discipline, and reserve build remaining contained.
tts_summary: Let's wrap up the morning earnings picture with Citigroup. The bank came in well ahead of expectations in the third quarter, posting earnings per share of two dollars and eighty-five cents against the Street's estimate of two sixty-five — that's a 27% year-over-year increase and a meaningful beat. Revenue came in at twenty-three point eight-five billion, just above the twenty-three point seven-two billion consensus, while expense controls were a real standout — the efficiency ratio improved 290 basis points to 59%, beating the Street's 60.7% estimate. Provisions were also slightly lighter than feared at two point five-eight billion versus two point six-five billion expected, and they only built three hundred sixty-nine million in reserves during the quarter, which signals management isn't particularly alarmed about credit quality. On the investment banking side, FICC revenue rose 4% to four point three-eight billion, coming in ahead of plan. Equities were up 14% to one point seven-two billion, a touch light versus the Street's one point seven-seven billion estimate, but not a concern given the broader strength. IB fees were a clear highlight — up 9% to one point three-five billion versus one point two-six billion expected, with equity underwriting surging 77% year-over-year. That's a strong signal on capital markets activity. Looking ahead, management raised full-year guidance on both net interest income — now seeing sales up in the mid-to-high 6% range versus the prior 5 to 6% guide — and return on tangible common equity, now targeted at 11% versus the prior 10 to 11% range. Both tweaks are modest but directionally positive and show confidence heading into year-end. Bottom line: this is a clean, solid quarter from Citigroup — beats on the top and bottom line, expense discipline, contained credit costs, and a guide that moves in the right direction. The investment banking rebound story remains intact, and this print should be well-received. Keep an eye on how the rest of the large-cap bank cohort trades on the back of this.
